shots.phrase: Begin by framing Foundations of Algorithm Analysis as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Algorithm analysis connects a precise problem specification to a correctness argument and resource bounds.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Asymptotic Notation Basics precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Big-O notation captures the worst-case growth rate of an algorithm's time complexity as input size increases.
A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
With the foundation in place, examine how Loop Invariants for Correctness operates in a concrete sequence.
A loop invariant supports a proof by initialization, maintenance, and termination.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in Divide-and-Conquer Strategy and make the decision criteria explicit.
Divide-and-conquer algorithms split a problem, solve subproblems, and combine their results.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Recurrence Relations to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Recurrences describe the cost of recursive algorithms.
Work from the concrete inputs to the result, checking units, types, or invariants at each step.
Examine the tradeoffs in Graph Algorithms Overview, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
Graph algorithms operate on vertices and edges to answer reachability, ordering, connectivity, and path questions.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Dynamic Programming Fundamentals with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Dynamic programming records solutions to overlapping subproblems.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Core Methods and Data Structures to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Core methods include sorting, hashing, trees, graphs, shortest paths, and dynamic programming.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Automata and Formal Languages to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Automata and formal languages describe machines, accepted strings, and computational limits.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Practical Analysis Checklist as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
A disciplined solution states inputs and outputs, proves correctness, and then analyzes time and space.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
